port_difficulty.why: Two lines of JCL. Its only step runs IEFBR14, the IBM do-nothing utility, with no DD statements, so there is no logic and no arithmetic to port.

blast_radius.why: Head of the nightly cycle, which the client said must not break. It waits on EXTERNAL-FEED, which nothing in the tree sets, and its JOBA-DONE condition is the only thing that releases JOBB. If the condition is lost in a port, the cycle stalls or runs out of order and the JCL gives no hint.

units.driving_fact: JOBA posts JOBA-DONE (OUTCOND +) and JOBB waits for it (INCOND), so the order lives only in the Control-M definition.

port_difficulty.why: The JCL is as trivial as JOBA's. The one subtle piece is in the scheduler: JOBB deletes JOBA-DONE (SIGN -) and posts JOBB-DONE, so the target scheduler must reproduce consume-and-delete condition semantics.

blast_radius.why: Second job of the must-not-break nightly cycle. Nothing in the tree consumes JOBB-DONE, so an unseen downstream consumer may depend on it. A missing or early JOBB-DONE would be silent, not an abend.

units.driving_fact: JOBB waits for JOBA-DONE, deletes it when done, and posts JOBB-DONE, which no job in the tree waits on.
